summary: The first mismatch originates before the queue annotation teleport.c:collect_coords. When a gremlin-form hero falls into a pool, trap.c:drown() takes its successful rn2(3) split branch and calls potion.c:split_mon(&gy.youmonst, NULL). JavaScript trap.js:drown() had replaced that call with note_unported("mon.c split_mon"). Restoring the canonical split_mon() call reaches mhitu.c:cloneu() and then the existing makemon.c:makemon() hero-square relocation. A fresh replay exposed a second source-traced guard mismatch: makemon_create.js:preflightCreation() rejected the clone call at its initial POOL square before C-equivalent enexto_core() relocation. The cloneuCall shape now bypasses that generic ACCESSIBLE preflight, and the admitted recording matches completely.

source.branch: In trap.c:drown(), after hero inventory water_damage_chain(), if u.umonnum == PM_GREMLIN and rn2(3) is nonzero, C calls (void) split_mon(&gy.youmonst, NULL). The helper’s canonical definition is potion.c:split_mon(); its hero branch calls cloneu() when u.mh > 1, divides current and maximum HP between hero and clone, sets disp.botl, and prints "You multiply!" only when a clone is returned. C’s mhitu.c:cloneu() invokes makemon() at the hero square with NO_MINVENT|MM_EDOG|MM_NOMSG. C makemon.c:makemon() relocates that runtime hero-square request through enexto_core() before placement checks. The existing JS makemon port recognized cloneuCall for runtime continuation and species admission but omitted it from preflightCreation()’s generic inaccessible-square rejection; this task adds that exact source call shape to the exemption so the C relocation branch runs.
callers: The selected production path is ordinary hero movement into a pool: hack.c:pooleffects() calls drown() and consumes its relocation boolean; js/hack.js:pooleffects() awaits js/trap.js:drown().

Other existing direct JavaScript callers are already wired: trap.c:float_down() consumes drown() and js/trap.js:float_down() awaits it; do_wear.c:Amulet_off(), dothrow.c:hurtle_step(), and dbridge.c:e_died() discard the return. Their existing JS paths include do_wear.js and dothrow.js; dbridge.c:e_died() has no equivalent callsite in js/dbridge.js and is unrelated to the selected route.
dependencies: The canonical potion.c:split_mon() is implemented as js/potion.js:split_mon(); trap.c:drown() discards its return, so the caller need not consume it.

mhitu.c:cloneu() is implemented as js/mhitu.js:cloneu() and consumes makemon()’s returned pointer; that callee is already source-mapped in js/makemon_create.js. The scoped makemon correction changes only preflightCreation() admission for cloneuCall and leaves the existing relocation/runtime implementation intact.

C makemon.c:makemon() computes byyou from the hero coordinates, then calls enexto_core() before the sanity and occupancy checks. Its C source does not reject the requested hero square by ACCESSIBLE terrain before that relocation.
The selected entry reaches trap.c:drown() through hack.c:pooleffects(); existing water_damage_chain() and terrain-entry wiring precede the gremlin branch.

guardCorrection.branch: else if (byyou && !gi.in_mklev): enexto_core(..., gpflags), then retry without GP_CHECKSCARY if needed; return NULL only when both searches fail.
guardCorrection.javascript: js/makemon_create.js:preflightCreation() recognizes cloneuCall from mhitu.c:cloneu() arguments. The generic non-mklev ACCESSIBLE guard must exclude that exact call shape so makemon() reaches its existing hero-square relocation.
guardCorrection.evidence: scripts/makemon-create.test.mjs pins source order and exercises a cloneuCall at POOL with eight adjacent ROOM squares.

selectionReason: Selected from combined queue SHA-256 188a7c5a196444733f454016c73ff5587f9bf9ce71a94c48b17d3683d62422df, evaluated against 47ce6cdb703dac648a39587abe9512daf2ee2e50. evidence: The immutable queue entry records batch v47, case v47-gremlin-pool-split, manifest SHA-256 b2ac7c3343f7e6fadd7d4e1c9fa090c162858739e1259555965cfa81d01cb608, recording SHA-256 cec2aac1f4630221ca4cba8708f20db1a2ebe82d18391e4b42c7c782fbaed8cd, evaluation challenges/evaluations/accepted-47ce6cdb703dac648a39587abe9512daf2ee2e50-v47.json from 47ce6cdb703dac648a39587abe9512daf2ee2e50, and a first mismatch at segment 0 step 37 on key space. C reports rn2(8)=4 at collect_coords(teleport.c:700); screen cell row 5 column 29 is a green gremlin in C and floor in JS.

The recording uses seed 47001012, debug Monk with pettype:none, polymorphs the hero into a gremlin, wishes for a pool, then moves into it while overloaded. Step 37 follows water-damage inventory processing and has C rn2(3)=2 at drown(trap.c:5088), followed by the collect_coords shuffle and later “You multiply!”; the second gremlin appears at row 5, column 29.

Upstream trap.c:drown() at lines 5059-5200 calls (void) split_mon(&gy.youmonst, NULL) in its PM_GREMLIN branch at line 5089. The helper’s canonical definition is potion.c:split_mon() at lines 2873-2935; its hero branch calls cloneu() and emits the multiplication message only on successful clone creation.

Current js/trap.js:drown() at line 1417 substitutes note_unported("mon.c split_mon") for the source call. js/potion.js:split_mon() and js/mhitu.js:cloneu() already provide the source helpers. Therefore C enters clone placement and consumes teleport.c:collect_coords RNG while JS never reaches that downstream path.

After the two scoped corrections, `node scripts/diff-fresh.mjs challenges/cases/v47/v47-gremlin-pool-split-attempt6-pager-resume.recipe.session.json` passes exactly: 2714/2714 PRNG values, 39/39 screens and 39/39 cursors (bounded run-47NyHt). The C clone request begins at the hero’s pool square, is relocated to accessible terrain by makemon.c:makemon(), and the replay completes through the session’s final boundary.
